title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic redeploys Claude Fable 5 globally with deeper cyber safeguards, a jailbreak severity framework, and a HackerOne cyber-bounty
bullets.summary: Fable 5 (longest-autonomy model) came back online globally July 1 across the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork, now wrapped in stronger cyber controls and a public researcher bounty for cyber jailbreaks.
bullets.how: Fable 5 is The Construct's advisor/judge and hardest-work tier; the redeploy stabilizes that tier, but the imminent shift to usage-based credits means reserve Fable for long-autonomy reasoning and route routine scans/drafting to Sonnet 5 to protect margin.

bullets.title: xAI's Grok 4.3 lands on Amazon Bedrock at $1.25 / $2.50 per 1M tokens, 131K context
bullets.summary: Grok 4.3 is now a first-class Bedrock model at aggressive pricing, giving AWS-native shops a cheap frontier option alongside Claude and Gemini.
bullets.how: Our stack is Claude-centric, but a sub-$3 blended frontier price on Bedrock is a useful fallback/benchmark for cost-sensitive client deployments where we don't control the tenancy.

bullets.title: X launches a hosted MCP server — read-only agent access to posts, users, conversations, and trends via the user's own account
bullets.summary: Announced June 30, it lets Claude/Cursor/Grok connect to X and search posts, read content, look up users, and analyze conversations/trends in real time with no write access and no separate API keys.
bullets.how: A real, key-free social-signal source for Pulse and Mirror: B9/PRAGMA can wire brand- and competitor-mention monitoring on X into the agent ecosystem without buying X API access.

bullets.title: Perplexity's CTO signals a shift away from MCP toward APIs and CLIs, launching a multi-model Agent API
bullets.summary: Citing high context usage and auth friction, Perplexity is de-emphasizing MCP in favor of direct APIs/CLIs for agent integration.
bullets.how: A caution against building The Construct MCP-only; keep the integration layer protocol-agnostic (MCP where clean, direct API/CLI where MCP is heavy) so we're not exposed if protocol consensus wobbles.

bullets.title: arXiv 'agent harness engineering' hardens into a named field — survey work now catalogs 110+ papers and 23 systems
bullets.summary: Research consensus continues to shift agent capability away from the base model and toward harness design: orchestration, tool interfaces, memory tiers, and verification loops.
bullets.how: Extends July 4's harness theme; use the survey taxonomy to audit each Construct agent's orchestration/verification loop, since that layer — not the model — is our durable edge as models commoditize.

praxis_lesson: The moat keeps migrating to the harness and the integration surface, not the model. Fable 5's global redeploy plus Grok-4.3-on-Bedrock commoditize the model layer, while X's MCP server and Perplexity's API pivot show the integration surface diversifying. The Construct should treat its harness as the asset, stay integration-agnostic across MCP and direct APIs, and tier models ruthlessly — Sonnet 5 for volume, Fable 5 for long-autonomy reasoning.
